questions.note: Hallux longest and 3–5 descend, but the 2nd stops ≈12–13 mm behind the hallux (≈81 px plan, ≈72 px V4o at 6.2 px/mm; spec 3–5) and the 5th stands free beside the 4th, not curled under it. The toes have pulps and knuckles, yet in plan they are slender knobbly fingers with gaps, from below ring-banded stalks, and their creases are single hard ridges.

Order and heights are right: lateral apex ≈76 and medial ≈88–90 by eye in V8, the medial further forward (V4, plan). But the lateral malleolus is a long soft swelling with no tip, the Achilles stands off its hollows only below z≈90, and there is no anterior ankle crease at all: the front of the ankle is one broad fillet with no tendons.

defects.what: 2nd toe tip stops 12–13 mm behind the hallux tip (≈81 px in plan, ≈72 px in V4o, at 6.2 px/mm) against the 3–5 mm the spec allows; the toe line falls away steeply from a dominant hallux.
defects.fix: Lengthen toe 2 or relax its curl so its tip sits 3–5 mm behind the hallux; toes 3 and 4, now ≈21 and ≈35 mm back, can come forward a few mm with it.

defects.what: From above, toes 2–5 are slender (≈13–15 mm across), knobbly fingers with bead-like swellings on both sides of the PIP joints, set ≈2–3 mm apart and ≈6 mm from the hallux, with dark clefts between them.
defects.fix: A boot-wearing man's lesser toes are plumper and lie side by side, touching at pulps and knuckles; the PIP shows as a dorsal knuckle, not a ring swelling. Fill the toe widths and close the gaps.

defects.what: The 5th toe stands apart from the 4th with a visible gap, points straight ahead and sits level beside it; it is not curled or tucked under the 4th.
defects.fix: Adduct and flex the 5th toe so its tip lies partly under the 4th's middle phalanx, the nail turned 30–45° to face laterally.

defects.what: The 1st MTP medial eminence is a small, sharply bounded knob (≈6×9 mm here) with a concave neck in front of it, reading as a bunion or exostosis; it is as clear in V1f and the plan.
defects.fix: Make it a broad, smooth convexity (radius ≈14 mm) that flows straight into the hallux's medial side with no neck between them.

defects.what: From behind the heel is a box: vertical, parallel sides ≈71 mm apart from z≈13 to z≈54, square shoulders where it meets the Achilles, tight lower corners and a flat back face.
defects.fix: A real heel is a rounded bulb: its back face narrows upward to the ≈25–30 mm tuberosity at the insertion and rolls into the plantar pad, so its outline from behind is a broad U, not a rectangle.

defects.what: The lateral malleolus is a symmetric soft swelling ≈44 mm tall, fullest at mid-height and tapering gently both ways with no tip; in V3 it barely reads at all.
defects.fix: Build the pointed, lower, posterior prominence (24 mm dome, 5 mm proud): fullest low, ending in a defined tip with a hollow beneath it and the peroneal groove behind.

defects.what: The front of the ankle is one large concave sweep (radius ≈85 mm) from z≈140 into the dorsum, met only at ≈50% L; the outline still stands ≈98 mm high at 40% L, and there is no anterior ankle crease at z 80–84.
defects.fix: Keep the shin line nearly straight down to z≈90–100, then turn into the dorsum in a much tighter bend at the crease height (z 80–84), the instep falling away from there.

defects.what: The extensor tendons show only on the forefoot and fade out mid-dorsum; across the front of the ankle there is no tibialis anterior, EHL or EDL relief at all.
defects.fix: Run them continuously from the shin under the retinaculum: tibialis anterior as a 9 mm cord medial at the crease, EHL and the EDL fan lateral to it.

defects.what: From below, toes 2–5 are thin stalks with flat ring-like bands at their creases and ball-shaped tips, separated by deep gaps; no row of toe pads sits against the ball and there is no sulcus.
defects.fix: Real plantar toes are short, plump pads in a row just ahead of a deep sulcus that parts them from the metatarsal pad; their creases are folds in the pad, not bands.

defects.what: The medial midfoot is a flat wall with an isolated dark pit at about z 25; no navicular tuberosity reads where the spec puts it (z 42, 12 mm dome, 2 mm proud), and the arch hardly reads.
defects.fix: Raise the tuberosity as a low dome and let the arch read as a long, shallow hollow below it, edged by the soft roll of abductor hallucis; remove the pit.

defects.what: The 5th metatarsal styloid is a small round marble on the lateral border, sharply ringed by shadow, reading more like a ganglion than bone.
defects.fix: Make it a low tuberosity elongated along the border, merging backward into the line of peroneus brevis toward the lateral malleolus.

defects.what: A thin straight vertical line runs down the skin below the medial malleolus, like a mesh seam or cut.
defects.fix: Remove it; the skin there is continuous.

defects.what: The hallux IP crease is one hard ridge-and-step across the dorsum, like a ring or seam; it also shows as a collar in the plan.
defects.fix: Real skin over the hallux IP joint folds in 2–4 soft, shallow transverse wrinkles that fade toward the sides.

defects.what: A small, sharp pinched fold sits on the lateral sole near the 5th metatarsal base.
defects.fix: Smooth it into the continuous pad of the lateral column.

ranked: [D2] From above the lesser toes read as slender, knobbly fingers set apart with dark clefts between them; a boot-wearing man's toes are plumper, pressed side by side and short-looking. It is the plan view's biggest giveaway.

[D1] The 2nd toe stops ≈12–13 mm short of the hallux (spec 3–5), and toes 3–4 trail as well (≈21 and ≈35 mm), so the toe line drops steeply from a dominant hallux instead of the gentle Egyptian slope.
[D5] From behind the heel is a rectangle with square shoulders and parallel sides; a real heel is a rounded bulb that narrows up into the Achilles.

[D7] The front of the ankle is one soft, oversized fillet from z≈140 into the dorsum, so the ankle reads like a sock or a cast; there is no crease, and the instep next to the ankle is overfilled (≈98 mm high at 40% L).
[D9] From below the toes are matchstick stalks with ring bands and ball tips; real plantar toes are a row of plump pads behind a deep sulcus.
[D4] The 1st MTP knob has a neck in front of it and reads as a bunion; the real medial eminence is a broad, smooth swell.
[D6] The lateral malleolus is a long, soft swelling with no tip; a specialist looks for the pointed, lower fibular tip with a hollow beneath it.
[D3] The 5th toe stands free beside the 4th rather than curled and tucked under it.
[D8] Tendons appear only on the forefoot and vanish at the ankle; the tibialis anterior, the strongest landmark at the front of a lean man's ankle, is missing.
From behind, the Achilles stands off its hollows only below z≈90 and fades into a broad rounded back of the ankle above; on a lean man the cord and its hollows carry on well up toward the calf.
[D10] The medial midfoot is a flat wall with a stray pit: no navicular tuberosity and almost no readable arch in the medial view.

The sole is one smooth slab: no metatarsal pad swelling under the heads, no lateral column pad, and from below the arch is a narrow straight trough with a hard rim from heel to ball, more moulded insole than foot.
In front of the lateral malleolus the dorsum is an empty slope: no extensor digitorum brevis belly and no sinus tarsi hollow, both normal landmarks on a lean man's foot (V3, V1f).
[D11] The styloid reads as a round marble under the skin rather than a low, elongated tuberosity.

Declared and not scored, but it distorts the judgement: the vein relief is rope-like and crosses the dorsum and medial ankle in hard ridges, hiding the dorsum's dome and the medial malleolus's outline.
[D13] The hallux IP crease is a single hard ring-step; real skin there folds in a few soft wrinkles.
[D12] A thin seam line runs down the skin below the medial malleolus.
[D14] A small pinched fold mars the lateral sole near the 5th metatarsal base.
